title: My God, How Wonderful Thou Art
description: My God, How Wonderful Thou Art in Tonic Solfa to WESTMINSTER: the solfa with the words, staff notation, the seven verses, and a piano.
about: Frederick William Faber wrote the words, published in 1849. James Turle’s tune WESTMINSTER dates from 1835; Hymns Ancient and Modern sets the words to it.
underlay: My God, how won-der-ful Thou art, Thy maj-es-ty how bright, How beau-ti-ful Thy mer-cy-seat, In depths of burn-ing light!

lines: My God, how wonderful Thou art,
How dread are Thine eternal years,
By prostrate spirits day and night
The sight of Thee must be,
Oh, how I fear Thee, Living God,
And worship Thee with trembling hope,
Yet I may love Thee too, O Lord,
For Thou hast stoop’d to ask of me
The love of my poor heart.
No earthly father loves like Thee,
Bears and forbears as Thou hast done
Prostrate before Thy Throne to lie,
And gaze and gaze on Thee!
